newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam, China pledge cooperation on problems.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, China pledge cooperation on problems.

text.p: Chinese Politburo member Qiao Shi and Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet pledged a spirit of friendship and cooperation in working on problems dividing their two countries, Vietnam's official media reported on Tuesday.
"The two agreed to solve all remaining problems between Vietnam and China by negotiations based on equality and friendship," the daily Vietnam News said.
The reports did not refer specifically to border differences or competing claims on two island chains in the South China Sea.

Qiao, chairman of China's National People's Congress and a member of the Politburo's Standing Committee, told Kiet in Hanoi on Monday that Beijing wanted to boost cooperation with Vietnam for economic gains and regional stability.
Qiao is the second top-level Chinese official to visit Vietnam since June, which diplomats say might signal a phase of warmer bilateral relations.
The two communist countries have a long history of distrust resulting from alternating periods of peace and conflict.
Beijing's forces invaded in 1979 to punish Hanoi for its invasion of Cambodia. The brief but savage war that ensued cost at least 20,000 lives.
Tension over competing claims to sovereignty over the potentially oil-rich Paracel and Spratly islands has bubbled beneath the surface despite normalisation of relations in 1991.
In 1994, the two sides agreed to set up a group of experts to discuss their problems in the South China Sea.
Brunei, Taiwan, the Philippines and Malaysia have also staked claims to all or part of the Spratlys. China has occupied the Paracels since 1974.
